status: Native ICE/RTC connectivity observed in a disposable Chrome profile; application delivery unverified

browser.versionEvidence: Installed official application bundle; owned process launched this binary. No isolated-window version UI capture.
browser.environment: Same Mac; fresh disposable profile, no copied user profile, no sign-in or extension installation

scope: One user-started native trickle loopback, two peer connections in one page, dummy data, no external ICE servers or media; no complete-SDP test.

instrumentation.explanation: The added inline module is incompatible with the retained script-src self CSP. Original external candidate observer and process logging remained functional. No browser console CSP error was captured; this cause follows from served source and policy.

eventTimeOrigin: Seconds since diagnostic controller startup, not click time.

interpretation.connectivity: Both peers connected at 2, 8 and 12 seconds, with one remote candidate and one candidate pair each.
interpretation.resolver: Two internal resolver successes; one retained distinct-name OS result resolved IPv4. The older observer does not retain a deduplication count.
interpretation.permission: Two no-need-to-request permission branches; no permission change or denial observed. This is not evidence that the permission factory was absent.
interpretation.applicationDelivery: Unverified: channel-open and dummy-frame receipt markers were not retained.
interpretation.normalProfile: Untouched in this pass; its current behavior was not retested.
interpretation.rootCause: A disposable profile connected in a newly launched process; earlier normal-profile runs failed. The normal profile was not retested at the same time, so the difference may reflect profile, process or runtime state, or a change over time. No causal variable has been isolated.
interpretation.candidateApiLimit: remoteApi remained zero even in this successful connection; use remoteStats and pairs for the retained connectivity discriminator.

cleanup.evidence: Operator created the owned stop sentinel after reading six candidate snapshots. Original launcher used the same owned_process_stopped label for stop sentinel and process exit; the retained action history disambiguates the trigger.

limitations: Not a clean variable-controlled profile comparison; process, defaults, field-trial/runtime state and launch flags differ.
No proof of application data delivery, encrypted HP2P UI behavior, separate-tab Chrome, cross-device/WAN connectivity or anonymity.
No raw process lines, hostnames, addresses, ICE credentials or user browsing history retained.
